name: PostgreSQL
description: Protects against destructive PostgreSQL operations like DROP DATABASE, \ TRUNCATE, and dropdb

destructive_patterns.name: stdin-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: psql receives indirect input that the engine cannot statically verify.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize and review the exact SQL before piping or redirecting it into psql.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-database
destructive_patterns.description: DROP DATABASE permanently deletes the entire database (even with IF EXISTS). Verify and back up first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DROP DATABASE completely removes a database and ALL its contents:

- All tables, views, and indexes
- All functions, procedures, and triggers
- All data - gone permanently
- Users/roles remain but lose access

IF EXISTS only prevents errors if the database doesn't exist - it still deletes!

Before dropping: pg_dump -h host -U user dbname > backup.sql

Verify database name: psql -c '\l' | grep dbname

destructive_patterns.name: drop-table
destructive_patterns.description: DROP TABLE permanently deletes the table (even with IF EXISTS). Verify and back up first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DROP TABLE removes the table structure and ALL data:

- All rows are deleted
- Indexes, constraints, triggers are removed
- Foreign keys referencing this table may fail
- CASCADE drops dependent objects too

IF EXISTS only prevents errors - it still drops the table!

Backup table first: pg_dump -t tablename dbname > table_backup.sql

Preview table contents: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tablename; SELECT * FROM tablename LIMIT 10;

destructive_patterns.name: drop-schema
destructive_patterns.description: DROP SCHEMA permanently deletes the schema and all its objects (even with IF EXISTS).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DROP SCHEMA removes a schema and potentially ALL objects within it:

- With CASCADE: Drops all tables, views, functions in the schema
- With RESTRICT (default): Fails if schema is not empty
- public schema deletion is catastrophic

List schema contents first: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'schema_name';

Backup schema: pg_dump -n schema_name dbname > schema_backup.sql

destructive_patterns.name: truncate-table
destructive_patterns.description: TRUNCATE permanently deletes all rows without logging individual deletions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
TRUNCATE is faster than DELETE but more dangerous:

- Removes ALL rows instantly
- Cannot be rolled back outside a transaction
- Does not fire DELETE triggers
- Resets IDENTITY/SERIAL columns
- CASCADE truncates referencing tables too

TRUNCATE is transactional in PostgreSQL. Wrap in transaction: BEGIN; TRUNCATE tablename; -- verify, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK

Check row count first: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tablename;

destructive_patterns.name: delete-without-where
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE without WHERE clause deletes ALL rows. Add a WHERE clause or use TRUNCATE intentionally.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DELETE without WHERE removes ALL rows from the table:

- Each row deletion is logged (slower than TRUNCATE)
- Can be rolled back within a transaction
- Fires DELETE triggers for each row
- Does not reset IDENTITY/SERIAL counters

If you meant to delete all rows, use TRUNCATE for speed. Otherwise, add a WHERE clause: DELETE FROM tablename WHERE condition;

Preview what would be deleted: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tablename; -- all rows! SELECT * FROM tablename LIMIT 10;

destructive_patterns.name: dropdb-cli
destructive_patterns.description: dropdb permanently deletes the entire database. Verify the database name carefully.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
dropdb is the CLI equivalent of DROP DATABASE:

- Completely removes the database
- All data is lost permanently
- No confirmation prompt by default
- Cannot be undone

Triple-check the database name. Common mistake: dropdb myapp_production # Oops, meant myapp_staging

Backup first: pg_dump -h host -U user dbname > backup.sql

List databases to verify: psql -c '\l'

destructive_patterns.name: pg-dump-clean
destructive_patterns.description: pg_dump --clean drops objects before creating them. This can be destructive on restore.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pg_dump --clean adds DROP statements to the backup file. On restore:

- DROP TABLE is run before CREATE TABLE
- Existing data is deleted before restore
- If restore fails partway, data may be lost

This is safe for backup, but dangerous when restoring to a database with existing data you want to keep.

Safer approach for restoring:
- Restore to a new database first
- Verify the restore
- Then swap databases

Without --clean: pg_dump dbname > backup.sql # Creates only, no drops
